 Key points
 The Kerala High Court ruled directly recruited District Judges with a postgraduate law degree get three advance increments from 1 July 1996 
 A 2013 Government Order had limited the benefit to officers appointed after 22 November 2013; that part is quashed 
 The benefit covers directly recruited judges with the degree whether they joined before 22 November 2013 or after 
 Judges promoted from the subordinate judiciary, and direct recruits without a postgraduate law degree, are not covered 
 The High Court's Registrar had told the Government there were "less than ten officers" in the 1996–2013 group 
 Advertisement
 Ernakulam, 26 October: Directly recruited District Judges in Kerala who had a postgraduate law degree at entry are entitled to three advance increments from 1 July 1996, not from 22 November 2013, the Kerala High Court has ruled.
 A Division Bench of Justice Devan Ramachandran and Justice Basant Balaji, in a judgment dated 28 September 2026, allowed a former High Court judge’s appeal and quashed the part of a 2013 Government Order that made the benefit prospective only. It ordered the benefit for the appellant “and similarly placed officers”.
 The case so far
 The appellant was directly recruited as a District Judge from the Bar in 1995 with a postgraduate law degree; he became a High Court judge in 2012 and retired in 2015.
 The First National Judicial Pay Commission — the “Shetty Commission” — recommended in its report of 11 November 1999 that Civil Judges (Junior Division) with a postgraduate law degree get three advance increments, with the monetary benefits payable only from 1 July 1996. The Supreme Court approved its recommendations with modifications in 2002, but not this one.
 Kerala accepted the recommendations by order of 28 March 2007 but confined the benefit to officers appointed after that date. It took a court fight by the then serving Munsiffs and Magistrates, won in 2010 and upheld on appeal, for the Government to give them the three increments from 1 July 1996.
 The High Court’s Registrar asked the Government on 17 July 2013 to extend the same benefit to directly recruited District Judges. The Government agreed by its order of 22 November 2013, but made it apply only to those appointed after that date.
 What the government argued
 The Government’s letter of 12 May 2014 said the benefit was “not as a matter of right but leniency”, and that neither the Shetty Commission nor the Padmanabhan Commission had recommended such increments for the higher judiciary. The High Court replied on 16 September 2015 that there were “less than ten officers” in the 1996–2013 group. A Single Judge dismissed the writ petition in 2018, holding the Government could fix a date for a new benefit.
 What the court held
 The Division Bench held that what the Government granted in 2013 “was not a new benefit, but an adjunct of the recommendations of the Shetty Commission Report”, so the Single Judge’s finding that it could fix a cut-off “becomes untenable”. The Government’s stand that the benefit was leniency and not a matter of right could not be approved “in any manner”, it said. On the pay of judicial officers, the two institutions “must act cohesively and in the spirit of collaboration”, the Bench added. An earlier Single Judge judgment had already settled that the 2013 order was not limited to officers who joined after its date; the only surviving question was from when.
 “Consequently, we allow this appeal and set aside the impugned judgment of the learned Single Judge,” the court said, also quashing the Government’s contrary letters.
 Judges promoted from the subordinate judiciary and direct recruits without a postgraduate law degree are not covered. The judgment does not say what the increments are worth in rupees or by when the arrears must be paid.
 Source: High Court of Kerala at Ernakulam, WA No. 181 of 2019 (A.V. Ramakrishna Pillai v. State of Kerala), judgment dated 28 September 2026 (2026:KER:75152).

 Critical AdSense behaviour: adsbygoogle.push({}) does NOT bind to
 a specific . It says "process the next unbound in DOM
 order." So if you push N times, AdSense binds the first N 
 slots it finds.
 Live investigation (2026-05-29) showed the right sidebar still
 loading late on indianpaycalculator.in. DOM order of :
 1. LEFT sidebar (in aside.ad-sidebar-left)
 2-5. Display banners (4× AdBanner inside page content)
 6. RIGHT sidebar (in aside.ad-sidebar-right, after main slot)
 7. Mobile anchor (StickyAnchorAd at body end)
 Previously this script pushed twice (one per sidebar). Those 2
 pushes bound LEFT + Display#1, NOT LEFT + RIGHT. The other 5
 slots only got bound as AdBanner.client:visible islands hydrated
 on scroll — meaning the right sidebar was bound 6th, after the
 user scrolled past every in-page banner. That's the "right side
 opens very late" complaint.
 Fix: push once per SSR'd ad slot. AdSense binds them all in DOM
 order at body parse end — no React hydration wait, no scroll-to-
 view wait. Subsequent React useEffect pushes (from AdUnit /
 StickyAnchorAd) become no-ops since the AdUnit effect skips when
 data-adsbygoogle-status is already set. --> component was removed 2026-05-29 to eliminate the
